security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples, local Playwright URLs, mocked network calls, or Markdown formatting false positives. The bundled with-server helper is a real command-execution risk because it starts caller-supplied server commands with shell=True and then runs a caller-supplied command. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The server helper starts user-provided server strings with shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Replace shell=True with explicit argument parsing, or require server commands from a trusted allowlist or project configuration.

remediation.issue: The helper executes arbitrary trailing command arguments after server startup.
remediation.suggestion: Document that server and test commands must be reviewed and trusted before running in a workspace.

remediation.issue: The skill documentation encourages direct helper-script invocation for browser testing.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short safety note telling agents and users to inspect helper scripts and generated commands first.

content.value_statement: Weak tests slow releases and hide regressions. This skill guides test strategy, TDD, automation, coverage review, and Playwright web checks.
actual_capabilities: Designs unit, integration, end-to-end, smoke, regression, performance, security, and accessibility test strategies.
Provides TDD red, green, refactor workflows for several common programming frameworks.
Shows patterns for mocks, stubs, spies, fixtures, factories, parametrized tests, and snapshot tests.
Guides Playwright browser automation for dynamic web applications and static HTML pages.
Helps plan CI/CD quality gates, coverage thresholds, and test pipeline stages.
Includes examples for console logging, element discovery, screenshots, and server lifecycle testing.
limitations: It does not replace project-specific domain knowledge or acceptance criteria.
The bundled server helper executes local commands and should be used only with trusted inputs.
Examples require developers to adapt selectors, ports, paths, and framework commands.
It does not provide hosted test infrastructure or automatic coverage collection.

use_cases.title: Plan Feature Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Create balanced unit, integration, and end-to-end coverage for a new feature before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Web App Tests
use_cases.description: Improve Playwright tests by inspecting rendered pages, selecting durable locators, and adding reliable waits.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Release Gates
use_cases.description: Define CI test stages, coverage thresholds, and quality gates for pull requests and main branch releases.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test plan for this feature. Include unit, integration, and end-to-end coverage with priority levels.

prompt_templates.title: Write Focused Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Write tests for this module using the existing framework. Use arrange, act, assert and include edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Apply TDD Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through red, green, refactor for this behavior. Start with one failing test and keep changes minimal.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Web Test Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this web test suite. Identify flaky selectors, missing waits, coverage gaps, and CI gate improvements.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for a checkout flow.
output: A prioritized test plan covering cart validation, payment outcomes, tax rules, and order confirmation.
Clear separation between fast unit tests, service integration tests, and critical end-to-end paths.

output_examples.output: A review identifying unstable selectors, missing network waits, shared state risks, and fixture cleanup improvements.
A red, green, refactor sequence that begins with one failing behavior test and expands through edge cases.

best_practices: Start from the behavior and write the smallest test that proves it.
Keep tests isolated, deterministic, readable, and fast enough for frequent execution.
Review helper scripts and local commands before running them in a project workspace.
anti_patterns: Do not write implementation first when the goal is strict TDD.
Do not depend on test order, shared state, or external services without controlled doubles.
Do not run generated server commands until a developer has reviewed the command text.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows for software testing tasks.

faq.question: Can it write tests for any framework?
faq.answer: It is framework-aware, but users must provide project context and installed tooling details.

faq.question: Does it include Playwright guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes browser automation patterns, element discovery examples, and web testing references.

faq.question: Can it run local development servers?
faq.answer: It includes a helper script for server lifecycle testing, but commands should be reviewed before execution.

faq.question: Does it enforce coverage thresholds automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps define thresholds and CI gates, but project tooling must enforce them.

faq.question: Is it suitable for TDD?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides red, green, refactor guidance and test-first development patterns.
